overview: From 2026-11-08 to 2026-11-15, ethereum-optimism/optimism had 30 new PRs (10 merged), 7 new issues, and 35 active contributors.

topIssues.title: kona-client: the library cannot be built for a no_std target
topIssues.author: yoshidan
topIssues.body:
`kona-client`'s library side — `fpvm_evm`, `interop`, `single` — never references `kona_std_fpvm`; only the two binary sources, `src/kona.rs` and `src/kona_interop.rs`, do. But `kona-std-fpvm` and `kona-std-fpvm-proc` are declared unconditionally in `[dependencies]`, so cargo builds them for the library too. `kona-std-fpvm` reads the preimage oracle over file descriptors (`std::fs::File`, `std::os::fd`) and carries no `#![no_std]`, so a consumer that wants only the library cannot build for a `no_std` target:

```
error: `std` is required by `kona_std_fpvm` because it does not declare `#![no_std]`
```

No feature avoids it today: `client-tracing`, the only one, enables `kona-std-fpvm/tracing`.

We hit this building an Intel SGX enclave. The OP Stack light client in [datachainlab/optimism-elc](https://github.com/datachainlab/optimism-elc) uses `kona_client::fpvm_evm::FpvmOpEvmFactory`, and the enclave is built for a custom `x86_64-unknown-unknown-sgx` target with `-Z build-std=core,alloc`, where no `std` exists at all.

`kona-client` is also absent from `no_std_packages` in `rust/justfile`, so `just check-no-std` does not cover it.

### Proposal

Move both dependencies behind a new `fpvm` feature, gate the two `[[bin]]` targets on it with `required-features`, and have `client-tracing` enable it. `default` still enables `client-tracing`, so the ordinary build is unchanged; only a consumer that opts out with `default-features = false` sees a difference. Adding `kona-client` to `no_std_packages` would keep it from regressing.

We have this working against `kona-client/v1.9.0` and are glad to open the PR if the approach looks reasonable.

topIssues.title: op-deployer: measure forge's peak memory instead of trusting forgeRunMemory
topIssues.author: sebastianst
topIssues.body:
Follow-up to #23664, part of #23300.

op-deployer limits concurrent forge runs per host by memory, using a hard-coded estimate of one run's peak memory on contracts-bedrock: `forgeRunMemory = 1536 << 20` ([slots.go:42](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/blob/06b0ae6b1c7749041601097dcde0deb4cdca0720/op-deployer/pkg/deployer/forge/slots.go#L42)). `slotCount` divides the container's memory limit by it ([slots.go:44-52](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/blob/06b0ae6b1c7749041601097dcde0deb4cdca0720/op-deployer/pkg/deployer/forge/slots.go#L44-L52)).

Nothing keeps that value current. When contracts-bedrock grows, the real peak exceeds the estimate. Then too many forge runs share a CI container, and jobs are OOM-killed as flakes instead of failing with a clear message.

### Proposal

Measure the peak, and fail a test when it nears the estimate:

1. After `cmd.Run()` in `execWithEnv` ([client.go:429](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/blob/06b0ae6b1c7749041601097dcde0deb4cdca0720/op-deployer/pkg/deployer/forge/client.go#L429)), read forge's peak RSS from `cmd.ProcessState.SysUsage()` (`syscall.Rusage.Maxrss`, KiB on Linux). Log it at debug level with the script name.
2. Expose the peak to tests, and assert in a test that runs a real contracts-bedrock script. For example, one of the live runs in `integration_test/apply_test.go`. It should fail when a run exceeds about 90% of `forgeRunMemory`, and the message should give the measured value to bump the constant to.

### Done when

- A forge run's peak memory is logged.
- A test that runs in CI fails before the estimate goes stale.

🤖 *Co-created with Claude Opus 5.5*

topIssues.title: [BP-CM] contracts-bedrock: support bridge hooks on interop chains
topIssues.author: maurelian
topIssues.body:
A bridge hook and interop cannot be enabled on the same chain today. OPContractsManagerV2 rejects attaching a hook to a chain with `INTEROP` enabled, `OPContractsManagerMigrator.migrate` rejects chains whose portal has a hook, and op-deployer rejects `bridgeHook` together with `useInterop`.

There are two problems to solve:

- **A hook only covers its own chain's portal.** In an interop set, ETH and tokens move directly between L2s, and all members share one `ETHLockbox`. Value can enter through another member's portal and reach the hooked chain without passing its hook. One way to close this is to require the same hook on every member of the set, so the set has a single entry point to screen, and to keep attaching, replacing and removing the hook consistent across all members.
- **Interop's own messages go through the hook.** Some interop functions send messages through the portal: `L1CrossDomainMessenger.syncETHLiquidityPause` and `relayUndeliveredMessage` send deposits to L2, and the `UndeliveredMessageExporter` sends withdrawals to L1. The portal treats them like user deposits and withdrawals, so the hook acts on them too, and interop breaks if they are not delivered as sent. These messages should bypass the hook, for example by having the portal skip it for messages the protocol itself sends.

topIssues.title: op-devstack,op-reth: unify the duplicated test seams of the reth v2.6.0 coverage stacks
topIssues.author: einar-oplabs
topIssues.body:
## Summary

The two test-coverage stacks for the reth v2.6.0 bump (#23385 proofs-history ExEx, #23386 the rest) were written in parallel and grew near-duplicate devstack and op-reth test seams. Once both stacks are in, these should be unified so op-devstack carries one of each.

## Duplicates

- **Log capture.** The proofs stack added `RecordLogLines` (used by the proofs-history acceptance tests to watch op-reth's output for pruner and engine lines); the non-ExEx stack added `RecordLogs` with the `LogObservable` seam on `op-devstack/stack/logs.go` and `op-service/logpipe`. One recorder with one interface should serve both.
- **Workload helpers.** `newWorkload` and the account/contract fixtures that drive a proofs-history follower (`rust/op-reth/tests/proofs/core/window_helpers_test.go`) and the acceptance packages' own workloads overlap; one shared helper in the proofs e2e utils or in the DSL would do.
- **Flush cadence types.** The ExEx test module has its own copy of the live tests' `FlushCadence`; a thresholds struct in the trie crate (behind `test-utils`, or replacing the two positional `u64`s of `EngineHandle::spawn_with_thresholds`) would remove it (noted in #23449).
- **Store wrappers and snapshots.** `StoreWithHooks` (liveness test), the model test's store wrapper and the live tests' `DiskSnapshot` each wrap the proofs store for observation; one wrapper with hooks would cover all three (noted in #23451 and #23455).

## When

After the 24 PRs merge, as one or two upkeep PRs, so the merge order of the stacks does not have to change. Each duplicate is listed with the PR that introduced it so the cleanup can cite them.

## Related

- #23385, #23386 (the two coverage trees)
- #23428 (`RecordLogLines`), #23436 and #23440 (`RecordLogs` / `LogObservable`), #23449, #23451, #23455

topIssues.title: op-acceptance-tests: local build-deps skip the MockSP1Verifier artifact the devstack deployer needs
topIssues.author: einar-oplabs
topIssues.body:
## Summary

Since #23868 (2026-11-04) the devstack deployer always deploys `MockSP1Verifier` (`op-deployer/pkg/deployer/opcm/mock_sp1_verifier.go`, called from `op-devstack/sysgo/deployer.go`'s `DeployImplementations` stage). Its artifact comes from `packages/contracts-bedrock/test/dispute/zk/MockSP1Verifier.sol`, which `just build-no-tests` (`forge build --skip "/**/test/**"`) never compiles.

Every local acceptance entry point builds the contracts that way:

- `op-acceptance-tests/justfile` `build-deps` (behind `just test` and `just acceptance-test`)
- `rust/op-reth/tests/justfile` `build-contracts` (behind `just test-e2e-sysgo`)
- `docs/ai/acceptance-tests.md` step 2 and its "stale contracts" troubleshooting entry

So a fresh checkout fails every sysgo test at setup:

```
failed to read MockSP1Verifier artifact: failed to open artifact "MockSP1Verifier.sol/MockSP1Verifier.json": open MockSP1Verifier.sol/MockSP1Verifier.json: no such file or directory
```

Checkouts that ever ran a full `forge build` keep a stale copy of the artifact in `forge-artifacts/` and do not notice. CI builds the contracts separately and is unaffected.

## Fix options

1. Build the one test contract the deployer needs after `build-no-tests`, e.g. a `build-devstack-contracts` recipe that runs `build-no-tests` and then `forge build test/dispute/zk/MockSP1Verifier.sol`, and point the two justfiles and the doc at it.
2. Move `MockSP1Verifier.sol` out of `test/` (it is deployed to dev chains, so it is not only a test helper).
3. Drop the `--skip` for local builds and accept the longer compile.

Option 1 keeps the local build time and makes the dependency explicit.

## Reproduction

```
git worktree add ../fresh origin/develop && cd ../fresh
cd packages/contracts-bedrock && just install && just build-no-tests && cd ../..
just build-rust-release
go test -count=1 -run TestProofsHistoryFollowerServesMatchingHistoricalProofs ./op-acceptance-tests/tests/proofs_history_match/
```

topPRs.title: op-deployer: run forge on contracts bundles without the AST
topPRs.author: sebastianst
topPRs.body:
Merge after #23664: this PR is based on its branch.

A forge run of an op-deployer script peaked at about 1.5 GB and 3 CPU-s, because at start forge parses the artifact of every file in the script's build, AST included, and the AST is about 80% of the artifacts' bytes. op-deployer now runs forge only on artifacts without it:

- `mktar` strips the AST from the embedded and published bundles. It also drops the Solidity files outside the build and the library files other than sources, licenses and forge configs.
- A `file://` locator to a local build, as sysgo and op-e2e use, is copied the same way. The copy is made once per build into `bundles/` of the cache directory (`--cache-dir`, by default `~/.op-deployer/cache`), and the processes that use it share it:
  - one copy of contracts-bedrock takes 3.8 s and 4.6 CPU-s (48 MB RSS, 44 MB on disk), and a later process finds it in 7 ms;
  - processes that start together copy once (a per-build lock);
  - eviction keeps the four most recently used copies and never removes one in use.
- An http bundle from an earlier `mktar` is copied the same way, into a directory of the process.

Measured on the `file://` local build, 12 CPUs, transparent huge pages on:

| | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| Peak RSS per forge run | 1.52–1.61 GB | 0.34–0.37 GB (0.20 GB without THP) |
| `TestEndToEndApply` | 65.5 s (25 forge runs: 41.5 s, 73 CPU-s) | 51.9 s (28.2 s, 35 CPU-s) |
| sysgo world build, `TestRPCConnectivity`: its one forge run | 1.56 GB, 2.0 s | 0.35 GB, 1.5 s |
| Embedded `.tzst` | 18.7 MB | 2.5 MB |

The bundle stays warm: no op-deployer script compiles on it. `forge verify-contract` on it submits the same sources as before: I compiled each submitted standard JSON with solc, and it matches the artifacts' bytecode. Only the remappings that forge auto-detects from `lib/` differ, and no source uses them.

**Forge slots.** The slots now count memory only: three quarters of min(cgroup limit, `MemTotal`), at 1.5 GiB per run.
- Before, a host without a cgroup limit had no memory bound, only cpus/2.
- 1.5 GiB still fits a run on artifacts with an AST, for example a local directory that can't be copied, so the sizing stays safe for every bundle.
- Slot counts: 8 on a 16 GB CI container (was 4), 11 on this 22 GB host (was 6).
- No CPU term, because oversubscribing CPUs costs nothing: 24 runs on a stripped bundle took 3.7 s at 6 at a time, 2.1 s at 12 and 2.2 s at 18. On AST artifacts it was 7.9 s at 6–9 and 11.8 s at 12, as memory ran short.

**What a copy takes from the project.** A bundle is code and data that scripts with a deployer key read, so a copy holds only files of the project:
- every read goes through an `os.Root` of the project and checks that it read the file the walk found;
- a copy never contains a link. A link that is, is in, or holds part of the build (the artifacts, the build infos, `forge-artifacts/` whatever the compile cache says, the compile cache, the forge configs and the sources) makes op-deployer use the build as it is, where #23664's `checkFsPermissions` refuses it. Paths are compared ignoring case, so the result doesn't depend on the filesystem. Every other link is skipped;
- only builds whose artifacts are in `forge-artifacts/` are copied;
- `.env*` files and directories are left out.

The shared directory and each stored copy must be private directories of the user, not links. Lock waits end after 5 minutes. Whenever op-deployer falls back to a private copy, or to the build as it is, it logs a warning with the reason.

A copy's key covers the project's path, compile cache and forge config, but not the artifacts' content. Hitting that gap would take a second build with an identical compile cache, source mtimes included.

**Behaviour changes worth checking:**
- A deployment prepared with a `file://` or http locator by an earlier op-deployer no longer continues, because the stripped artifacts have a different content digest.
- A cache directory that other users can write holds no copy: each run then copies the build into a temporary directory and logs a warning. The tests that use the local build share one private cache directory in TMPDIR, so the integration tests copy it once instead of 36 times.

Copying the bundle once per CI pipeline, in the contracts build job, is left for a follow-up. The workspace attaches at the checkout, not at `$HOME`, so it needs changes to the CI config and a command that packs the bundle, and one copy costs only 3.8 s per job.

Reviews: `go-code-reviewer`, seven rounds, and three security reviews. Its findings are fixed except two:
- the empty lock files stay, two per build, so that waiting processes lock the same file;
- an http bundle is copied a second time instead of being stripped in place.

Closes #24000

🤖 *Co-created with Claude Opus 5.5*

topPRs.title: op-reth: test that pool admission and the payload builder agree
topPRs.author: geoknee
topPRs.body:
Pool admission and the payload builder were only tested separately. This adds property tests that run a real validator and pool and the real builder against the same head, L1 info, base fee, balance and nonce, on both Jovian and Karst, plus parity tests for the two FastLZ implementations in use.

It also aligns the validator with the limits these tests exercise. 

The pool rejects a transaction above these limits at submission, with the existing "exceeds maximum per-transaction gas limit" error. For a DA footprint, the first number in that error is the footprint. Block validity doesn't change.

topPRs.title: contracts-bedrock: screen and complete deposits through the bridge hook
topPRs.author: lumoswiz
topPRs.body:
**Description**

Enables the bridge hook to allow, reject, or hold deposits in `OptimismPortal2`. Only the configured hook can complete a held deposit, preserving its original terms and restoring its ETH or token backing. The L1 ProxyAdmin owner bypasses screening so governance can always reach L2.

Completions share the block’s deposit gas limit with ordinary deposits without paying the resource fee again. Chains without a hook retain existing behavior.

**Tests**

Adds coverage for screening, holds, completion, failed restoration, duplicate completion, reentrancy, governance bypass, and upgrades. A metering invariant checks that mixed deposit flows stay within the block’s gas limit.

**Metadata**

- Closes ethereum-optimism/optimism-private#739

topPRs.title: kona-engine,kona-node-service: import delegated local-safe and cross-safe heads separately
topPRs.author: einar-oplabs
topPRs.body:
Under interop op-node imports a delegate's local-safe and cross-safe heads separately; kona-node copies the delegated safe head into both, so its forkchoice safe hash can run ahead of cross-chain verification.

Kona-node now follows local-safe for the EL lookup, EL sync and reorgs, and moves the safe label to cross-safe only when it advances. Chain identity, not the code path, decides between extending and reorging: local-safe is compared with the EL block at its height (or the unsafe hash at the unsafe height), and a cross-safe head that differs from local-safe is checked against the EL's header. A diverged head reorgs, moving safe back to cross-safe; when the EL lacks the block only the advance rule applies. A cross-safe head behind finality leaves just the safe label in place. Before interop both heads are one block, so non-interop chains see no change and no extra lookups. The kona-node configuration docs and `--l2-follow-source` help describe the labels and the interop caveat.

BREAKING CHANGE: `ConsolidateInput::BlockInfo` is replaced by `Delegated(Box<DelegatedSafeHeads>)`, built with `DelegatedSafeHeads::try_new`; the `From<L2BlockInfo>` conversions are removed.

Closes https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/issues/23911. Stacked on #24004.

|----------------|------:|--------:|-----:|
| Implementation |   454 |     192 |  262 |

topPRs.title: contracts-bedrock: screen and complete withdrawals through the bridge hook
topPRs.author: lumoswiz
topPRs.body:
**Description**

Enables the bridge hook to allow, reject, or hold withdrawals in `OptimismPortal2`. It receives the selected proof's finalizable time so it can wait for clearance before holding.

Only the configured hook can complete a held withdrawal, restoring its backing and executing its original call once, with the original L2 sender and required gas. Failed target calls leave withdrawals held for retry. Chains without a hook retain existing behavior.

**Tests**

Adds unit and fuzz coverage for screening, finalizable time, holds, completion, replay protection, failed calls, gas limits, pause and reentrancy guards, and unsafe targets. Also checks token custody call ordering and preservation of held withdrawals across upgrades.

**Additional context**

Builds on #23736.

Lowers the Portal's optimizer runs from 750 to 200 to make room for the withdrawal path.

**Metadata**

- Closes ethereum-optimism/optimism-private#740
